title: A trained transformer approximated Heavy-Ball updates without examples of them
summary: A theoretical and numerical study found that a simplified transformer for linear regression can shift from imitating gradient descent to approximating the known Heavy-Ball method. It first learned gradient-descent trajectories and was then trained against the true regression weights, without Heavy-Ball trajectories as supervision. The proof concerns later steps under specific initialization, parameter and high-dimensional data assumptions. The result appeared in arXiv v1 on October 22.

source_review.scope: arXiv version history, v1 introduction and v2 model, theorem, assumptions and experimental comparisons

evidence.tested: The analysis proves approximate Heavy-Ball behavior in later steps of a trained regression model under stated assumptions. Numerical experiments compare the transformer trained in two stages with gradient descent, Heavy-Ball and single-stage transformer training.
evidence.unknown: The result concerns a simplified transformer and controlled linear regression. It does not establish the same training dynamics for frontier language models or arbitrary optimization problems.
evidence.ai_role: A transformer trained in two stages produces the trajectory being characterized; no examples from the Heavy-Ball update rule were supplied as supervision.
